<div class="page-intro">

I lead by making the decision clear, creating room for expertise and keeping the team accountable for the outcome. I want people to understand what matters, why it matters and where they have the freedom to decide.

My approach rests on five commitments: set direction, develop people, build for scale, turn evidence into decisions and protect analytical integrity.

</div>

---

## Leadership principles

::: {.leadership-grid}

::: {.leadership-card}

### Set direction

I turn ambiguous business needs into a clear problem frame, measurable outcome and prioritized roadmap. I test assumptions early, make trade-offs explicit and align stakeholders on scope, ownership and decision criteria.

**In practice:** I have aligned Product, Commercial, Engineering, BI and Analytics teams around shared metrics, delivery priorities and executive review mechanisms.

:::

::: {.leadership-card}

### Develop people

I set clear expectations, align responsibilities with individual strengths and development goals, and remove obstacles without prescribing every step. Direct, respectful challenge is welcome; people should leave a discussion with both clarity and ownership.

**In practice:** I have led multidisciplinary analytics and data science teams whose specialists needed autonomy in their craft and shared accountability for the business result.

:::

::: {.leadership-card}

### Build for scale

I look beyond the immediate analysis to create capabilities other teams can reuse: common definitions, automated reporting, self-service tools and recurring decision processes.

**In practice:** I have scaled KPI reporting, led BI automation and established analytical frameworks used across products, markets and teams.

:::

::: {.leadership-card}

### Turn evidence into decisions

I translate business questions into analytical work, then translate the evidence back into choices, implications and recommendations. I adapt the detail to the audience without hiding uncertainty or trade-offs.

**In practice:** I have guided decisions on marketing experiments, product roadmaps and cross-functional launches, helping technical and non-technical leaders work from the same evidence.

:::

::: {.leadership-card .leadership-card-wide}

### Protect analytical integrity

I make assumptions, limitations and uncertainty explicit. Metric definitions, validation and causal claims should be rigorous enough for the importance and reversibility of the decision—not more elaborate than the decision requires, and never less reliable.

**In practice:** I have owned business-critical metrics developed by my teams and established measurement standards that supported consistent interpretation across functions.

:::

:::

::: {.team-expectations}

## What teams can expect from me

- Clear priorities, ownership and decision rights
- Accountability without micromanagement
- Direct, respectful feedback
- Space to challenge assumptions
- Work aligned with strengths and development goals
- Pragmatism about when to reuse, adapt or build
- A clear connection between analytical quality and business value

:::
